problem_summary.summary: Treat each root-to-leaf digit path as a decimal number and return the sum of those numbers.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a non-empty binary tree with digit-valued nodes. Return the integer sum of all root-to-leaf numbers.
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer

brute_force.explanation: Build the digit value for every root-to-leaf path, store all completed values, then sum the list.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Each leaf contributes exactly one root-to-leaf number, and decimal accumulation by multiplying the prefix by ten and adding the next digit gives the represented path value.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — every node is processed once, then each leaf value is summed once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(l + h) auxiliary for l leaf numbers and the recursion stack.

optimized.explanation: Carry the current number down the tree and add it directly to the total when a leaf is reached, avoiding a separate list of leaf values.
optimized.correctness_idea: The carried value is the exact decimal number encoded by the path from the root through the current node. Adding it once at each leaf counts every root-to-leaf number exactly once.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each node is visited once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(h) auxiliary recursion stack; no leaf-value collection is retained.

Prefix multiplication naturally preserves the represented numeric value without a leading-zero special case.
